pass_a_gloss: Bel, dragon, sun, moon refused with Daniel and Job's hand-kiss rule.
pass_b_english: Not only images of gold and silver must we refuse, but every creature besides the Creator: sun and moon and stars, and Bel the Babylonians' idol, and the dragon — which Daniel refused, though commanded by the king to worship. 'I worship nothing,' he said, 'but the Lord my God.' And Job's word: 'If seeing the sun shining, or the moon full, my heart secretly rejoiced, and I kissed my hand to them' (Job 31:26–28) — reckoning star-worship as denial. So we: though the persecutor point to sun, moon, host of heaven, or Bel, or dragon, or emperor's image — we worship the Lord alone.
